validated_results.title: Zinc supplement use and risk of aggressive prostate cancer: a 30-year follow-up study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of 47,240 men reporting zinc supplement use with multivariable Cox models for incident prostate cancer, including aggressive disease, providing a target-specific incidence estimate.

extraction.population: Men in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 47,240 men from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study were followed from 1986 to 2016.

cases.excerpt: During a median follow-up of 28.3 years, we documented 6,980 incident prostate cancer cases including 1,053 lethal and 1,143 aggressive.

effect_size.excerpt: However, compared to never-users, men who used supplement zinc more than 75 mg/day were at higher risk for lethal (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.16-2.66, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.001) and aggressive prostate cancer (HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.19-2.73, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.006). Similarly, men who took supplemental zinc for 15 or more years had a higher risk for lethal (HR: 1.91, 95% CI: 1.28-2.85, P<sub>trend</sub> <0.001) and aggressive prostate cancer (HR: 1.55, 95% CI: 1.03-2.33, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.004).

confidence_interval.excerpt: However, compared to never-users, men who used supplement zinc more than 75 mg/day were at higher risk for lethal (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.16-2.66, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.001) and aggressive prostate cancer (HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.19-2.73, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.006).

comparison.excerpt: compared to never-users, men who used supplement zinc more than 75 mg/day

design.excerpt: Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between zinc supplement use and incidence of prostate cancer.

timing.excerpt: Men reported their zinc supplement use at baseline and biennially thereafter.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Men reported their zinc supplement use at baseline and biennially thereafter.

validated_results.title: Exploring the Association between Gut and Urine Microbiota and Prostatic Disease including Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and Prostate Cancer Using 16S rRNA Sequencing.
validated_results.reason: The study examines gut and urine microbiota taxa (Lactobacillus) via 16S rRNA sequencing in existing prostatic disease rather than a nutritional exposure related to incident prostate cancer.
